hook_clip: Here's how to reverse engineer Perdoo from a written spec. Claude passed all nineteen checks, and found seventy-two gaps in my spec.
outro_clip: The full spec is free at personal software factory dot com. If you build it, tell me what broke. I'm Sam. See you tomorrow.

scenes.text: We gave Claude one Markdown file. It copies the part of Perdoo a small team actually uses. Quarterly cycles. Company and team objectives, with up to five key results each. Weekly check-ins with a value, a confidence call and a comment. And a cycle close that scores everything.

The core rule is progress and pace. Progress is how far a key result has moved from its start toward its target, with the same formula whether higher or lower is better. Pace compares that with how much of the quarter has passed. At least ten points ahead of the calendar is Ahead. More than ten points behind is Behind. Anything else is On pace.
cues: from its start toward its target

scenes.text: Claude built it in four phases, one prompt each. The foundation. Check-ins and target changes. Reminders, the Friday summary and closing a cycle. Then alignment, charts and export. After every phase, the acceptance checks ran in a real browser.

Here's what it built. The OKRs page on day fifteen of ninety-two, with the self-serve revenue objective at fourteen percent. Each key result gets a weekly chart against a dashed line for the expected pace. The Alignment view puts each team objective under the company objective it supports. On Monday at nine, the reminder job emailed only the two people with late check-ins. Closing the quarter scores each objective from zero to one, and carries Sign ten new partners into the next quarter. And on a phone, Ben's late check-in comes first.
In one final run, on a fresh database, all nineteen checks passed, along with one hundred and thirty-six automated tests.

But the more useful result is what broke. The test build exposed seventy-two places where Claude had to guess. An admin could deactivate themselves, or demote the last admin, and lock everyone out. Carrying key results forward could push the next quarter past the limit of five. And the weekly chart had no rule for a week with no check-in. Every gap is now fixed in the spec.
Passing every check isn't the same as production-ready. We didn't test production sign-in, real email delivery, a hosted scheduler, or hosting. The reminder job was run by hand, never by cron.

So is it worth building? Perdoo is free for up to five users. For ten users billed yearly, Premium is nine dollars per user per month, one thousand and eighty dollars a year, and Supreme is eleven dollars. If you want KPIs, strategy maps and reviews in one product, buy it. If you only need objectives, key results and check-ins without a per-user fee, build it.
Everything is in one file. The data model, ten rules, seed data, four phase prompts, and all nineteen checks, with the seventy-two fixes already in.
